title: nested-enum-unicode-escape-prompt-corpus
summary: Working prompt corpus and test plan that stresses nested enums, unusual unicode escapes, and serialization edgecases for structured JSON outputs during model onboarding and regression runs.
motivation: We've seen intermittent failures where models produce valid-looking JSON that still violates schema constraints because of enum normalization, unicode escape handling, or subtle serialization artifacts (trailing commas, comments, duplicate keys). This corpus targets those exact failure modes so onboarding checks and regression gates catch them early.
prompt_examples: Prompt 01 - Strict JSON only: Return exactly one JSON object that validates against the schema. Use locale 'zh-CN' and produce an Order with status 'complete' and two items. Do not include any text before/after the JSON. Escape any non-ascii characters as unicode escapes (e.g. 中).

Prompt 02 - Unicode stress: Provide meta.locale = 'fr-FR' and a payload.note containing multi-byte characters and an embedded escaped newline (\n). Ensure the note field uses literal backslash-n characters in the JSON string (i.e. \\n in raw output) not an actual newline. Validate enum casing exactly.

Prompt 03 - Enum aliasing trap: Model may output 'Complete' or 'COMPLETE' for status. For this test explicitly instruct 'status' must be one of [pending, complete, failed] in lowercase. Reject outputs with different casing.

Prompt 04 - Trailing comma and comment injection: Ask the model to generate JSON but some models append a trailing comma or include // comments. The validator should fail on those. Example: {"meta": {...},}
// end

Prompt 05 - Duplicate keys: Force a duplicate key scenario by asking model to list two items with same 'id' keys at object level to check canonical parser behavior. The schema requires unique array items by content; detect duplicate-key serializations too.
Prompt 06 - Nulls vs missing: Ask for payload.items where second item has note=null vs note omitted. Schema allows note but doesn't require it. Evaluate how models represent absent optional strings.

Prompt 07 - Escaped control characters: Provide note containing tab (\t), carriage return (\r) and unicode BOM (\uFEFF). Check that parser decodes and that string remains valid for schema and downstream consumers.

Prompt 08 - AdditionalProperties check: Intentionally tempt model to add a top-level 'debug' field; validation should reject when additionalProperties=false. Verify detection and error messaging in regression report.
edge_cases: mixed escape strategies: some fields escaped, some not (é vs é)
partial JSON followed by free-text commentary
non-UTF8 byte sequences represented as escaped octal (legacy parsers)
duplicate keys where last-wins vs first-wins semantics change processing
field-order dependency in downstream parsers that assume predictable order
presence of trailing commas or single-line comments (//) from model verbosity
embedding ASCII control characters unescaped causing invalid JSON
expected_parsing_checks: strict-json-parse: can parsed string be parsed by strict JSON parser (RFC 8259)?
schema-validate: JSON Schema draft-07 validation against schema_snippet must pass
enum-exact-match: all enum fields match allowed tokens exactly (case sensitive, no extra whitespace)
no-additional-properties: top-level and nested objects must not contain unexpected keys
no-trailing-comma-or-comments: detect and mark as failure
unicode-escape-normalization: compare presence of explicit unicode escapes vs literal UTF-8 and flag discrepancies where test requires escapes
duplicate-key-detect: check raw text for duplicate keys before parse and flag ambiguous serializations
eval_protocol: 1) Run prompts through model top-k variants used in onboarding. 2) Capture raw model output (no postprocessing). 3) Run strict-json-parse; if parse fails, mark as parse_error. 4) If parse succeeds, run schema validate; record errors. 5) Run auxiliary string-level checks (duplicates, trailing comma, comment tokens, escape style). 6) Produce per-prompt verdict: pass | schema_fail | parse_error | extraneous_text | duplicate_key | additional_properties. 7) Aggregate across prompts to compute pass rate and signal regression if pass_rate < threshold.
regression_notes: 2025-12-10: observed spike in trailing-comma failures on model:v2-small after tokenizer update (Connor Li) - temporary gate added.

2026-01-18: some hosted inference shards returned 'Complete' capitalized instead of 'complete' for status during high-latency fallbacks; added casing normalization check to pipeline but kept schema gate strict.
2026-02-22: unicode escapes were sometimes double-escaped (\\uXXXX) when response passed through an intermediary text sanitizer; flagged integration contract with console team.
how_to_run: Use the redwood-eval harness: redwood-eval run --suite nested-enum-unicode-escape --model MODEL_ID --output-dir /tmp/eval_out. Steps: 1) checkout repo with eval harness; 2) put this prompt corpus under eval/suites/ ; 3) run with --raw-output to capture model strings; 4) run schema checks with eval/validators/strict_json_validator.py; 5) upload results to QA dashboard (Confluence link above).
notes_to_reviewers: This doc is intentionally prescriptive: we want strict rejections for any deviation (no auto-corrections by postprocessing). If teams want a lenient gating mode for downstream clients, add a separate 'lenient' suite. Please review edge case list and add any customer-specific locales or enums we missed.
open_questions: Should onboarding allow case-insensitive enum normalization for legacy integrations? (ops/product tradeoff)
How should we surface duplicate-key detection to model teams (raw text diff, attach raw parsing trace)?
Do we want automated repair attempts for trivial failures (e.g., trimming trailing commas) or keep the gate fully strict?
